discoveredCase: A message carrying more than 10 message attributes, and a message whose body plus attributes exceed 256 KB
behaviorContract: The transport either splits, rejects or offloads a message that exceeds the AWS message-attribute count or total size limits, with a diagnosable error rather than a truncated message.
boundaries: 10 message attributes and 256 KB total are hard AWS limits.
negativeAndFailurePaths: Silent truncation is the failure being guarded.
oldExecutionState: NOT PRESENT - no inherited test covers this

notes: GAP - no inherited test. Discovered from current product surface per Lead plan §9 (second ledger input). Untested. External: LocalStack does not enforce the attribute count or the 256 KB payload ceiling, so a test written against it is green regardless of the product's behaviour - the classic 'emulator makes the test lie' case. It also determines whether the MessageData/S3 offload path is required. REQ-TEST-106 row.

No occurrence of RedrivePolicy, deadLetterTargetArn or maxReceiveCount anywhere in the SQS product project - so native SQS DLQ is not used. That is a design decision, not an omission, but it is undocumented and untested. The Lead should confirm the statement before it is asserted.

discoveredCase: A receive endpoint configured with a non-zero WaitTimeSeconds
behaviorContract: Long polling holds the ReceiveMessage call open for the configured duration instead of returning empty immediately, reducing empty receives while keeping shutdown responsive.
boundaries: 0 (short polling) and 20 (the AWS maximum) are the two boundaries; the harness default is 0 and one fixture sets 1.
negativeAndFailurePaths: A stop that has to wait out a 20-second poll is the defect guarded.
oldExecutionState: NOT PRESENT - no inherited test covers this
assertionIntent: With WaitTimeSeconds = 20 on an empty queue the receive call blocks for approximately that long and returns empty; a message arriving mid-poll is returned promptly; a stop request cancels the poll without waiting it out.
notes: GAP - no inherited test. Discovered from current product surface per Lead plan §9 (second ledger input). Set in three places and asserted nowhere. External: long-polling timing and the distinction between short and long polling are server-side behaviours; LocalStack returns immediately in both modes, so the property has no observable effect there. REQ-TEST-106 row.

discoveredCase: Configuring a visibility timeout above 12 hours and a renewal below 60 seconds
behaviorContract: MaxVisibilityTimeout is clamped to 12 hours and MaxVisibilityTimeoutRenewal is raised to 60 seconds, matching the AWS limits, rather than being passed through and rejected by the service.

discoveredCase: A FIFO endpoint with DisableMessageOrdering() called
behaviorContract: Calling DisableMessageOrdering turns off per-MessageGroupId partitioned delivery on a FIFO queue, so messages of one group may be processed concurrently.

negativeAndFailurePaths: The enabled case must still be strictly ordered; that half exists (Fifo_Specs) and the disabled half does not.
oldExecutionState: NOT PRESENT - no inherited test covers this

notes: GAP - no inherited test. Discovered from current product surface per Lead plan §9 (second ledger input). Public surface with zero call sites in the tests. ConcurrentDeliveryLimit has the same status.

discoveredCase: Batched publish, send and delete against SNS and SQS
behaviorContract: Operations are batched up to the AWS batch limits, a partial batch failure is reported per entry rather than failing the whole batch, and every entry is eventually accounted for.

negativeAndFailurePaths: A partial batch failure silently reported as success is the defect guarded.
oldExecutionState: NOT PRESENT - no inherited test covers this

Three public batcher types plus ClientContextBatchSettings and PublishBatchSettings, none of them tested. External: partial batch failure is an AWS response shape LocalStack does not reproduce faithfully, and the batch size and payload caps are not enforced there. REQ-TEST-106 row.
